From 13 s the cutting drops to 0.25-0.75 s for an effects exchange: M in a fire swirl, a white flash (13.9), sand blasts, M flying, light pillars, V CU (17.9), fire vortex and ring bursts, M's golden halo (20.4), sand wave, blue blast, flash (23.6), feet landing in sand (24.1), M standing in an energy burst (24.9-26.4). structure.ending: No fight resolution beat. After the dragons' explosion (281-283) comes an environment and damage montage. M and S are knocked back (298.1-300.9) and V's cracked chest jewel is shown with blood (292.6, 307.9). The coda is slow by this video's standard: two locked EWS holds of fiery clouds over a tiny V (302.9-307.9), V bleeding CU, a low-angle MS push, profile and frontal CUs, then a 3.2 s EWS that fades to black (317.4-320.6). It closes with a static multi-line end card from 320.6 to the end: the creator's statement (hand-drawn storyboards, prompt design, self-funded AI generation; original rights belong to the Pili studio; non-profit promotion) and a large subscribe line. Behind the card, recap clips cut under a dark overlay.

ai_handling.pattern: Cut length far shorter than a generation: most clips are trimmed to fragments
ai_handling.evidence: Visual median shot 0.5 s; 188 of 469 shots appear on only one 0.25 s frame; only 6 shots run over 3 s. Frame-level checks found 8-9 cuts in 49-52 s and about 17 in 133-137 s. A 5-10 s generation is almost never shown whole. The longest holds go to shots that do not need character acting: the dragon sigil (250.4-255.4), the palm turning into a tornado (89.1-93.1), and a slow push on V standing (221.6-225.4).

ai_handling.pattern: Effects and environment plates instead of character acting
ai_handling.evidence: 208 shots are effect plates (fire, gold or blue streaks, vortexes, mandalas, dragons) and 45 are pure environment. Together that is more than half the shots, all without a readable face or body performance. Fights are told as colour-coded energy (gold = M, blue = S, black/red = V) meeting in mid-frame.

ai_handling.pattern: Speaking mouths almost never carried on screen
ai_handling.evidence: Subtitled dialogue runs across about two-thirds of the shots, but faces get only 41 face shots and 4 eye ECUs, mostly 0.25-1 s. Long lines play over wides, inserts and effects. In the CUs checked with paired frames, the mouth is hidden by M's beard (1.1-3.1) or closed (V profile 314.6-316.1). Lip-sync cannot be judged in a muted pane, but no long talking-head shot exists.

ai_handling.pattern: Hands as poses and inserts, not as manipulation
ai_handling.evidence: Hands appear as large stylised inserts: a clawed hand rising (9.6), a palm with an orb forming (43.4-44.6, 162.9-164.1), a palm pushing at the camera (115.6), a bleeding hand (216.4-218.4). The hardest hand action, catching a sword between two fingers, is split into a fingers-raised insert (50.6) and a fingers-already-holding-the-blade MS (51.1-52.1), with no in-between motion shown.

ai_handling.pattern: Contact and hits shown by cut, insert, flash and reaction
ai_handling.evidence: The strike chain at 156.1-161.4 runs: sword in flight, blade insert, S thrusting, V's chest jewel, tip meeting the jewel inside an energy flare, S grimacing, the jewel glowing. Contact is never a two-body move. M's hit is a blood-spray CU (121.4) and his knock-back is tumbling wides (202.6-204.1). Clashes cut on impact frames: manga speed lines (102.1, 111.9), a white-black frame (129.6), an ink splatter (185.6), white and cyan flashes (115.4, 186.4). The only sustained two-shot of contact (211.9-213.6) is a locked push of a sword against the jewel, not an exchange of blows.

ai_handling.pattern: Identity kept by costume, colour and recurring inserts
ai_handling.evidence: Each character has a fixed silhouette and palette. V: black robes, silver headdress, red forehead jewel, turquoise chest jewel with beads. M: red and white robe, prayer beads, white hair. S: white robe, white hair, pointed ears, blue sword light. V's chest jewel returns as an insert (157.4, 159.9, 169.9, 199.9, 207.6, 292.6 cracked, 307.9 cracked) and doubles as the story's damage counter. Small figures in wides are read by colour alone.

ai_handling.pattern: Back, silhouette, low-angle and feet framings avoid face drift
ai_handling.evidence: V from behind or in silhouette (52.4, 139, 148.6, 154.4, 259.1), robe-hem and boot inserts (170.6-172.9, 293.4, 300.9-302.9), M's feet stepping and stomping (24.1, 112.4, 237.9), and OTS geography (7.4, 259.1).

ai_handling.pattern: Calm holds are wides or near-static CUs
ai_handling.evidence: The slow class covers only 11 shots, all locked: an OTS wide (7.4), empty desert (41.6), the blade beside the ear (149.4), a sand plume (173.9), a mountain (288.4), fiery-cloud EWS (302.9, 305.6, 317.4), a V profile CU (314.6) and the end card. The probe found no near-frozen frames (share 0), so even the holds carry cloud, dust or lightning motion. Whether some are image-to-video clips with mostly camera move cannot be told from frames.

craft_notes: Roll call before the fight: one ~1 s push-in per character (M 1.1, S 3.1, V 4.1), then one OTS wide from behind the villain to fix who stands where (7.4-8.9). Geography is set once and then dropped.

Strike grammar, from 156.1-161.4: weapon insert (sword flying) -> blade insert -> attacker MS thrust -> target detail insert (chest jewel) -> contact hidden in an energy flare on the insert -> attacker reaction CU (grimace) -> target detail reacts (jewel glows) -> target face CU, unfazed. Repeated at 205.4-213.6 with a locked two-shot as payoff.

Power-up grammar: palm insert -> effect forms in the palm -> wide of the effect taking over the landscape (43.4-44.6 then 44.6 flash; 89.1-93.1 palm to tornado in one take; 162.9-164.1 spiral in palm, then S struck at 164.4).
Impact punctuation: a 0.25 s impact frame (manga speed lines, white-black frame, ink splatter, white or cyan flash) between attack and result, at 102.1, 111.9, 115.4, 129.6, 185.6-186.6, 243.1.

Speed ramps by scene: about 1 s shots for the standoff, 0.25-0.5 s during barrages (40-53, 128-139, 148-158), back to 1-3 s holds for the invocation wides (245-268) and the coda (301-320). In the fastest passages a frame-level check found a cut every ~0.2 s.

Colour coding replaces faces in action: gold streak = M, blue streak = S, black/red = V. A 0.25 s streak shot reads as a specific character's move (100.4-101.9 gold and blue dashing in parallel; 130-136).
Reaction and damage beats use blood plus distance: blood-spray CU (121.4), blood at the mouth CU held 1 s (201.6, 298.6), then the body tumbling small in a wide (202.6-204.1).

Climax built as an escalating wide ladder: feet stomp insert (237.9) -> mandala FS -> light pillar tilt (241.9) -> beam insert -> sky vortex EWS -> Sanskrit mandala EWS -> dragons emerge (5 s, the longest shot, 250.4-255.4) -> villain looks up CU (255.4) -> OTS villain vs the dragon ring (259.1) -> dragons dive -> explosion EWS (281.1).

The aftermath is told with environment and objects, not people: mountain, shockwave dome, mushroom cloud, cracked glowing ground, cracked jewel with blood (283.4-296.4). Then short reaction beats of each hero staggering (298.1-300.9).
The coda slows down: locked EWS holds of 2-3 s, the cracked-jewel insert, bleeding CU, a low-angle MS push, two CUs, and an EWS fade to black (301-320.6) before the end card.

Burned-in subtitles carry the dialogue the whole way (about two-thirds of shots), so picture and line are decoupled: lines run over wides and effects, and short 3-4 character move-name callouts land on the attack shot (for example on the fire burst at 10-12).
2.33:1 scope frame throughout: wide desert compositions with small figures and big sky effects suit the format.
videos.sound_and_text: The pane was muted, so nothing here is about audio. Burned-in text: (1) White subtitle lines without a box, centred low in the frame (about 0.80-0.86 of frame height), present over roughly two-thirds of the runtime. The 0.5 s subtitle-band sheets show long gaps only in pure-action passages (about 46-56, 88-101, 124-139 and 286-292 s). The lines read as character dialogue and self-introductions: the opening line is a character's title. There are also short 3-4 character move-name callouts on attack shots, for example a move name over the fire burst at 10-12 s. From 224 to 280 s a line is present on almost every frame, which reads as a continuous incantation or dialogue during the summoning. No separate poem card or name card was seen; the description's taglines appear only in the description, not as on-screen cards. (2) End card from 320.6 s to the end: a static multi-line paragraph block. It is the creator's statement: they are the original maker of this anime series, the work was copied by others, the original rights belong to the Pili studio, and the picture was made from hand-drawn storyboards, prompt design and self-funded AI generation for non-profit promotion. A large subscribe line sits under it, all over a dimmed recap montage. No captions track: meta().captions was empty. Description says the rights belong to the Pili studio and the picture is a personal new rendition; tags name 一頁書, 風之痕 and 棄天帝 (the three characters labelled M, S and V here).
caveats: Method change, stated plainly: the repo probe at step 0.25 s (as instructed) found only 217 cuts / 218 shots (median 1.25 s, p10 0.5, p90 3, longest 5, opening_10s 10, opening_30s 22, near_frozen_share 0, 1 failed sample). In this video almost every 0.25 s sample has mad >= 26 (928 of 1,329), so runs of flagged samples were merged into single cuts and most real cuts inside effect passages were lost. For example, 13-26.25 s holds about 22 visible cuts, while the probe counted 7. A second pass at 1/15 s over-detected badly (642 'cuts' from fire and flash flicker). The cut_times, shots and stats reported here therefore come from a visual pass over the whole video on 0.25 s contact sheets (25 pages, 54 frames each). Each cut sits at the midpoint between the last frame of the old shot and the first frame of the new one (±0.125 s), so lengths are effectively multiples of 0.25 s.

Visual cut list error: two frame-level spot checks (49-52 s and 133-137 s at 1/15-1/12 s) found that the 0.25 s list is about right in one place (9 listed vs 8-9 real; one 'cut' at 49.4 is probably a crash zoom) and undercounts in the other (14 listed vs about 17 real). Shots under 0.25 s, mostly flash and impact frames, are under-resolved. Treat 469 shots as ±15% and the median as 0.4-0.5 s.

Some listed cuts may be fast camera moves or effect morphs inside one generation, and some long shots may hide a cut. Examples: 26.4-28.4 changes angle (possible cut ~27.9); 89.1-93.1 has no frame-level spike but transforms completely; 151.9-152.1 (i257) may not be a cut.

Pane hidden: the first measurement in a background tab read the same frame for every sample (mad 0). Frames updated only after a screenshot made the tab render, so all numbers come from the second run. The zoom action is not supported in this pane, so labels come from cells about 133x57 px in the screenshots. Character identity in tiny wides is inferred from colour (gold = M, blue/white = S, black = V), and 'people' counts in wides are approximate.
Character names M, S and V are my labels. The description and tags name 一頁書, 風之痕 and 棄天帝, but the mapping is inferred from costume, not stated on screen.

motion_energy_mean is the mean 0.25 s-probe mad inside each shot, excluding the sample at the cut. For shots that span only one 0.25 s frame, it is the mean of the 1/15 s samples inside (basis says 'fine mad'), which is on a smaller scale. Several of those read 0-0.2 because consecutive 1/15 s samples hit duplicated frames, which suggests some clips run at a lower native frame rate. Those six shots were reclassified from paired frames (four active, two unknown).

Motion classes: by the probe thresholds almost every shot is 'active' (mean > 4), because effects, lightning flicker and particle motion inflate mad. 11 shots were corrected to 'slow' from paired frames (locked framing, only cloud, dust or hair motion). No shot is frozen.

Subtitle presence per shot comes from 0.5 s subtitle-band sheets and is mapped to shots by time overlap, so 0.25 s shots next to a line boundary may be mislabelled. A pixel-based subtitle detector was tried and rejected because the bright sand and sky in the band defeated it.
Scene setups and returns are estimates: almost every shot is a fresh AI composition, so 'setups' is close to the shot count and returns are counted only where a composition clearly repeats.
No audio claims; dialogue/narration status is inferred only from burned-in subtitles. Lip-sync could not be judged.

ai_handling.pattern: Effects and empty environments carry much of the screen time

Step change: the requested 0.25 s pass found 155 shots (median 1.25, p10 0.5, p90 3.25, longest 9.0, opening_10s 7, opening_30s 15, near_frozen 0.016). The video was therefore measured again at step 0.125, which gave 287 shots. The reported stats, cut_times and shots[] come from that 0.125 pass.

The 0.125 pass is still approximate. It misses cuts in the densest montage (15.13-18 is one probe shot holding about 8 visible shots; a 0.25 s audit of 15-26.75 counted about 25 cuts against the probe's 15). structure.opening: First 10 s: no title card. 0-1.8 an extreme wide shot of a fortress on a volcanic peak over a red sea, with a tiny walking figure and one short subtitle line. 1.8-3.4 a tracking insert on feet and robe hem walking on red water. 3.4-4.9 a profile MCU of the white-haired lead in a black hood. 4.9-6.7 an insert of his hand counting prayer beads. 6.7-8.4 a slow-push MS that reveals him in full. 8.4-10.5 a demon-beast head whose eye ignites. The probe counts 6 shots in 10 s, and the hero is shown in pieces (feet, profile, hand) before the full reveal. 10.5-30 s: an EWS of him wading through the red sea under his name line (10.5-13); an ECU of his eyes (13.25); then the antagonist's power display: a fire ring (15), a wave (15.5), a whip-blur into a demon lord in lightning (16.9-19.4), a 4.75-s ground shockwave (19.5-24.25), a seated demon king push-in (24.25), and a figure flying at the burning fortress (25.25-27). scenes.what: Arrival: the fortress, the hero shown in pieces (feet, profile, hand with beads, MS), the beast's eye wakes, the hero wading in the red sea, an ECU of his eyes
The antagonist's power display: fire ring, wave, demon lord in lightning, ground shockwave, seated demon king, a figure flying at the burning fortress
The hero's first technique: rush in, hand-with-beads insert, gesture, the rosary whips around him, rings of beads as a seal on the sea, a glyph gesture, explosion, his silhouette in a storm

The demon realm answers: the fortress shot again, spires, a portal vortex, dunes, the hero standing, a face ECU, the demon king on his throne
Fight inside the vortex: the demon's core, spires with lightning, the hero facing a white vortex, red slashes and debris, red-wave cutaways, solo combat in a dark vortex, landing on the water
Interlude: the fortress, a blood orb, fog clearing, a tiny figure on the sea, a winged demon, a dip to black and a flash into a demon silhouette, giant waves
Transformation and duality: the hero from the front, a disk seal, a rune circle on the water, hair flaring with glowing eyes, a white-robed counterpart appears in two-shots, a flash, a halo

videos.sound_and_text: The pane was muted, so nothing here is claimed about voice, music or sound effects. Burned-in text comes in two kinds. (1) Single-line white Chinese dialogue subtitles, small, centred low in the picture. In the 0-30 s band sheet they run nearly continuously: lines change roughly every 1.5-3.5 s (about 0.5-3.5, 5-8.5, 9-11, 11.5-13, 14.5-18, 18.5-21, 21.5-23.5, 24-25.5, 27.5-29), with short gaps at about 4-4.5, 13.5-14 and 26-27, and they cross cuts freely. They read as character dialogue (lines address other characters by name), not narration or poem cards. Mid-frame checks show them through most of the video, including the fight passages. (2) A fixed two-line call-to-action end card during the outro (308-339.5) that recommends the original puppet drama and asks for likes and subscriptions. There are no poem or title cards and no name cards. meta().captions is empty (no caption tracks). The video description holds a poem-like passage, not transcribed here. caveats: The pane was muted. Voice-over, music and sound design are not verified; any lip-sync judgment is visual only.

The probe under-counts cuts badly in this video. Fight passages have constant high motion and a uniform gold and dark palette, so flagged samples form long runs that count as one cut, and histogram distance stays low across cuts. Re-measuring at 1/15 s gave 57 vs 38 cuts in 0-55, 125 vs 31 in 55-100 and 96 vs 33 in 205-250. Frame sheets at 0.15 s show about 14-16 real shots per 5 s in fights, while the fine pass over-counts flash effects by roughly 25%. A rough estimate of the true total is 350-450 shots: about 1-1.3 cuts per second overall and about 2-2.7 in fights. The probe's median of 1.25 s overstates shot length; fight shots are typically 0.2-0.5 s.

Then a strike chain cut every 0.3-0.6 s: arm thrust 3.3, over-the-shoulder beam toward the red demon 3.7, red masked CU 4.1, starburst impact 4.5, shockwave and smoke 5.1-6.1, cracked-ground aftermath 6.1, red boots walking 6.7, red demon MS 7.1, master MCU 7.5, gold flash frame 7.7, OTS two-shot 7.7-8.3, master CU with sword 8.5, crowned master 8.9. The first wide fight two-shot starts at 9.1. Burned-in lines start about 4.0 as short title-like phrases echoing the video title; a longer narration line announcing the battle runs about 7-10.5. First 30 s (55 shots by eye; the probe found 18): the clash runs non-stop with weapon, boot, fist and eye inserts between brief wides. The only breather is a 2 s tree-and-waterfall landscape (24.7-26.7). After it the crowned master gets a re-introduction: hilt insert 27.7, FS 28.9, sword-level MS 29.7, lotus aura 30.7.

ai_handling.pattern: No speaking mouths, no lip-sync
ai_handling.evidence: No shot shows a mouth forming speech. The only dialogue-like caption sits on a locked, static Luohou CU with the mouth closed, while only the clouds move. All other text is narration or verse. Faces otherwise appear as 0.25 s expression flashes (grin, gritted teeth) or as eye ECUs.

ai_handling.pattern: Contact replaced by flash + insert + reaction
ai_handling.evidence: Hits are never one continuous contact. The over-shoulder contact lasts one 0.25 s frame, then a white-gold burst, a blade-across-chest CU, a medallion ECU and the defender's spark eruption. Luohou being struck at 16.0 is a 0.25 s light burst. The whirlwind slash shows only the attacker inside a white vortex. The red-canyon two-shot is from behind, with no touch.

ai_handling.pattern: Sub-second cutting keeps every generation short
ai_handling.evidence: Fights cut every 0.25-0.5 s: 34 shots in 5.0-23.0 (median 0.5 s), and six consecutive 0.25 s shots in the speed blitz. The longest shot in the video is 4.75 s and the median is 0.75 s, so 5-10 s generations are evidently trimmed to their best 0.25-2 s. Character takes over 2 s are rare: the 4.25 s rise at 36.25, and 2.0-2.25 s dance shots.

ai_handling.pattern: Whiteouts and lightning as transition cover
ai_handling.evidence: Full-frame flashes sit at switch points (a personality switch, a new space, a reveal). Lightning flickers through most environment plates, which also hides plate-to-plate changes. The probe read lightning as cuts at 88.75, 107.0 and 121.75.

ai_handling.pattern: Identity anchored by recurring costume and prop inserts
ai_handling.evidence: Luohou: gold crown with winged ear guards, green hair, red eyes, chest medallion. Xiaori Biao: patterned cap with a studded band and a curved sword. Fengxiu: purple hair, tall black crown, feather fan with a red gem. These get their own ECUs and come back repeatedly. Each storyline also has a fixed colour world (moonlit blue snow, red maples with blue curtains, a red canyon).

ai_handling.pattern: Hands only grip props
ai_handling.evidence: Hands appear only holding the fan or the sword: one simple lift, a swing and a level hold. There is no finger work, no hand-to-hand contact and no object handover.

ai_handling.pattern: Dance shown through parts, plates and tiny wides
ai_handling.evidence: Full-body dance shots last 2.25 s at most, or the dancer is tiny in a wide. The rest of the choreography is robe-hem, feet and sleeve inserts, fan ECUs, and cutaways to storm plates. No long continuous full-body choreography is shown.

ai_handling.pattern: Near-still plates (likely lightly animated stills) for breathing room
ai_handling.evidence: Establishing and bridge shots use a locked camera where only mist, cloud, waves or lightning move. Probe mean mad is 2.7-5.5 for several of them, against 20-40 in action shots. They hold 1.5-4.75 s, the longest shots in the video.

ai_handling.pattern: Small figures in wides
ai_handling.evidence: Wides keep characters tiny or silhouetted, so face and costume detail never has to hold up at a distance.

I checked every one of the 304 disputed cuts on a paired-frame sheet, using a 1/24 s profile to find the jump and 4-frame context rows for the unclear ones. Of the 278 only-theirs cuts: 172 are real, 86 are false and 20 stay unresolved. Of my 26 only-mine cuts, 25 are false and 1 is real (262.25, a golden ring cutting to a lightning strike). In a sample of 27 matched cuts, about 17 are real and about 9 are false positives we share. That puts the true count at roughly 290-315 cuts, a mean shot of about 1.1 s. So they overcount by about 50% and I undercount by about 30%. Where their extra cuts are real, they come from the probe's run-collapse: in the 0.25-0.5 s montage stretches, back-to-back real cuts get merged into one, so my list misses them (e.g. 23.63, 30.63, 65.63, 97.38, 120.88, 307.88). Shot 403 is not a real shot (both its boundaries are in-shot). Shot 0's push-in can't be confirmed from the frames. Every label is motion 'active', including the calmest shot in the video (372), so that field carries no information.
notes: Their times are the midpoint between 0.25-s samples: their t equals my sample t minus 0.125 (147 of the 190 matches have an offset of exactly -0.12). Their boundaries are therefore good to about +/-0.13 s; three shot starts I checked frame by frame sit about 0.08-0.1 s before the true cut (24.13 vs about 24.23, 98.63 vs about 98.72, 160.63 vs about 160.71).

cross_check.verdict: Their cut list is closer to the truth than my probe's default output, but it is not reliable as given. Of their 138 cuts that I did not have, the 1/8-s strips show 68 to be real cuts within about 0.15 s and 9 more to be real cuts 0.2-0.45 s away. 40 are false: lightning flashes, a fire or explosion growing inside one shot, cloth wipes, or the same setup on both sides. 21 I could not decide at thumbnail size, mostly in the 46-56 s and 208-220 s sword fights. My probe badly under-counts this video. It found 154 cuts against their 286, because sustained high motion forms long runs of flagged samples and only the first sample of each run is kept: 19.75-26 s and 213.5-220.5 s each have zero probe cuts but 8 or more real ones. Of my 6 cuts they did not have, 116.25 is right, 192 is about 0.2 s late for a real cut at about 191.75, and 45, 93.75, 174 and 194 are false. Matching does not prove a cut: at least 6 matched pairs are false for both of us. The true cut count is probably about 220-260, so their mean shot of about 0.93 s understates shot length a little and my 1.72 s overstates it a lot. In 10 of the 15 labels I agree on size and subject, but several of their shot boundaries are wrong.
notes: The probe ran at 0-266.5 s, step 0.25, with no failed samples. The frame was 1280x548 (2.33:1 scope). Stats: 155 shots, mean 1.72 s, median 1.25 s, p10 0.5, p90 3.25, longest 9 s, 7 cuts in the first 10 s, 15 in the first 30 s. A preroll ad ended without needing a skip click.
Their cut times are on a 1/8-s grid (.13/.38/.63/.88), not the probe's 0.25-s grid, so they used a finer or different method. The mean offset of matched pairs is 0.07 s.

Matched pairs that are false for both of us, because the frames on both sides are one shot: 55.75 (top-down crater, 55.25-56), 76.25 (mountain with cloud ring, 75.875-77), 78.13/78.25 (cracked ground, 77.5-78.375; the real cut is 78.45, their 78.5), 117.75/118 (dark rock pillar, 116.25-118.125), 171.13/171 (flaming sword, 170.75-171.6), 227.88/228 (red figure with rings, 227.25-228.125; the real cut is their 228.13).

Real cuts that neither list has: ~24.35 and ~24.66 (gold face CU -> fire insert -> purple warrior), ~61.0 (gold face CU), ~82.6 (gold boots), ~94.45 and ~94.8 (in 94-95 s there are about 6 cuts; they have 3 and I have 2), and probably ~49.6.

Probe weakness worth fixing in the skill: cuts() treats a sustained run of flagged samples as one cut. In this extremely fast AI action edit that discards real cuts (63.5-65.5 is one run; 114.25 is kept while the real 114.5 cut is dropped). For videos like this, the default output should not be quoted without contact-sheet checks.

A 1/30-s frame-difference scan was tried as a tie-breaker for disputed cuts. It is noisy here: within-shot frame differences of 20-50 are common, and many zero diffs show held or duplicated frames. It was decisive only for 24.25, 25.25 and 40 (single spikes) and for 28.75 (no spike). Verdicts rest on 1/8-s and 1/16-s contact-sheet strips (17 sheets) and one paired sheet.
